sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:192867
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 29543 of 2024
Applicant :- Varsha

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Satyendra Narayan Singh,Vineet Singh Parmar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Vide order dated 25.11.2024 passed by Hon'ble the Chief Justice, the instant bail application has
been nominated to this Bench.
2.  Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that notice has been served to the informant of the case on 01.8.2024.
Despite service of notice none has appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Satyendra Narayan Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram,
learned AGA-I, for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release her on bail in Case Crime No.81 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376 AB, 302 and 201 IPC and Section 5M/6J-3(iv) POCSO Act, Police Station Gagalheri, District Saharanpur during pendency of the trial.

1 5.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged on 12.5.2024 under Section 363 IPC against unknown persons and according to the FIR, on 12.5.2024 in the afternoon, the daughter of the informant aged about 5 years had gone somewhere from her home but in spite of search she could not be traced.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that initially FIR of the present case was lodged under Section 363 IPC but when on 13.5.2024 dead body of the daughter of the informant was recovered then case was converted under Sections 302 and 376 AB IPC.

7. He further submits that during investigation when Investigating Officer recorded the second statement of the informant then he stated that Chaman Lal and Karan Pal informed him that on 12.5.2024 they witnessed Shubham along with the deceased while they were entering in the house of younger brother of the informant, namely, Vikas.

8. He further submits that from the second statement of the informant it also reflects that he was having suspicion that applicant, the wife of Vikas, was having illicit relationship with Shubham and only due to this reason firstly Shubham committed rape upon his daughter and thereafter he and applicant committed her murder.
9. He next submits that after second statement of the informant recorded during investigation applicant has been made accused in the present matter along with co-accused Shubham.

10. He next submits that when the statement of Chamal Lal, Karan Pal and Vikas, i.e., husband of the applicant, were recorded during investigation then they also reiterated the second statement of the informant.

11. He further submits, it appears that as these witnesses were having suspicion that applicant was having illicit relationship with co-accused Shubham, therefore, applicant has been made accused in the present matter along with Shubham.
12. He further submits that there was no occasion for the applicant to commit murder of the deceased rather there was reason of her false implication.
13. He further submits that surprisingly husband of the applicant, namely, Vikas has not been made accused in the present matter.

14. He further submits that dead body of the deceased was recovered from the vacant plot of one Nekiram and admittedly the dead body was not recovered either from the house of applicant or on her pointing out.

15. He further submits, the evidence that the deceased and Shubham were last seen while they were entering into the house of applicant also appears to be shaky and it appears that only due to this reason the informant, the elder brother of the husband of the applicant was having suspicion that applicant was having illicit relationship with co-accused Shubham, therefore, in his second statement he started making allegation against the applicant.
Varsha vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36183044/
2 16.

entities.text: Varsha vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that except suspicion there is no evidence against the applicant on record.

17. He next submits that applicant is a lady and she is not having any other criminal history and in the present matter she is in jail since 15.5.2024, i.e., for the last more than six months.
18.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits that it is a case in which five years old girl has been murdered after rape and there is also evidence that co-accused Shubham entered in the house of the applicant along with the deceased on the date of incident but could not dispute the fact that the dead body of the deceased was not recovered either from the house of the applicant or on her pointing out and it was recovered from the vacant plot of one Nekiram.
19.

Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that on the basis of same evidence, husband of the applicant has not been made accused and only applicant, who is lady has been made accused in the present matter.
20.

Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that it appears, except suspicion and motive,
there is no cogent evidence against the applicant on record.
21. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

22. However, it is a case in which five years old girl has been murdered and before murder her rape was also committed but applicant is a lady and from the entire evidence available on record it could not be reflected at this stage that she was also involved in the present crime.
23.

However, as per prosecution, co-accused Shubham was last seen with the deceased while they were entering into the house of applicant but all the witnesses stated that as applicant was having illicit relationship with co-accused Shubham and she is the 'bhabhi' of the informant and, therefore,
she committed the murder along with Shubham.
Considering this fact the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant with regard to false implication of the applicant, cannot be ruled out at this stage.

24. Further, deceased was the daughter of elder brother of the husband of the applicant and if applicant was having illicit relationship with co-accused Shubham then also it cannot be said that she was having motive to commit instant crime as there was no occasion for her to eliminate the niece of her husband.
25. Further, from the entire record, it appears, except suspicion, there is no cogent evidence against the applicant.
26. Further, applicant is a lady and she is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter she is in jail since 15.5.2024. i.e., for the last more than six months.

27. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

29. Let the applicant-Varsha be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless her personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
30. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

31. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
